text:
There is no comforting spin on the Canucks. Vancouver is 3-14-1 with seven points, winless in four and 1-8-1 over its last 10. Our simulations give them no realistic path to the playoffs and project 61 points. The question this season has quickly become what comes next.

The chances explain most of it. Vancouver has 40% of the expected goals and is giving up 3.81 per 60 minutes. Then the goaltending made it worse: 83 goals allowed against 69 expected, a 14-goal hole. Kevin Lankinen is 0-5-0 with a .802 save percentage over his last five starts, 9.3 goals worse than expected, and Leevi Meriläinen is at .847 over his.

Manny Malhotra called out the team's "lack of effort" after the lopsided loss in Winnipeg, as reported by Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis. We can't measure effort. We can measure that the pair of Filip Hronek and defenseman Elias Pettersson is at 37% of the chances and has been on for 11 goals against.

The good signs are small. Liam Öhgren has five points in his last 10. Jake DeBrusk and forward Elias Pettersson have broken even on goals with either Brock Boeser or Jonathan Lekkerimäki. Daily Faceoff asked whether it is time to "sell-high on Canucks' Elias Pettersson." On this evidence, the more pressing question is how much of the roster the Canucks want to keep.
headline: Seven points, and the numbers agree
